ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, and senior management must undergo comprehensive screening against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, and the domestic sanctions list maintained by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China. Additionally, Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) as defined by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) must be identified and subjected to enhanced due diligence. Screening must be conducted at the time of incorporation and on an ongoing basis. Any positive match triggers immediate reporting to the China Anti-Money Laundering Monitoring and Analysis Center (CAMMLAC) and may result in rejection of the application.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) - National Enterprise Name Registration System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Chinese characters. For foreign-invested enterprises, the name may include the foreign investor's name in Chinese transliteration. The name must follow the structure: [Administrative division] + [Distinctive name] + [Industry] + [Organizational form]. Phonetic transliteration must be consistent and not misleading. The name must not be identical or similar to existing registered names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name application is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the SAMR within 15 days of receipt of the rejection notice. The appeal must include a detailed explanation of why the name should be accepted, along with supporting documents. The SAMR will review the appeal within 30 days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may seek judicial review in the People's Court. The appeal process is governed by the Administrative Reconsideration Law of the People's Republic of China.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices and commercial mailboxes are generally not permitted for WFOEs in China. The registered office must be a physical location where the company can be contacted and where tax authorities and SAMR can conduct inspections. For e-commerce businesses, a virtual office is not accepted; a physical address is mandatory for registration and bank account opening. Failure to maintain a physical office may result in revocation of the business license.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) Verify physical presence of office equipment and staff; (2) Confirm the registered address matches the actual location; (3) Review business records and compliance with tax registration; (4) Inspect adherence to AML/CFT obligations. Risk: High likelihood (80%) of unannounced physical inspections by municipal tax authorities and SAMR within the first year of operation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act of Taiwan (R.O.C.), as amended; Articles 1, 2, 6, 98-100, 128-132, 156, 162, 185, 203, 205, 208, 210, 225, 229, 230, 235, 240, 387; Foreign Investment Act, Articles 4, 7, 8, 10; Regulations Governing the Permission of Foreign Investment; Act Governing Relations between Peoples of the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area, Articles 73 and 79; Company Registration Regulations; Business Tax Act, Article 28; Occupational Safety and Health Act for operational compliance.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan (R.O.C.), with the Investment Commission, MOEA serving as the foreign-investment pre-approval authority; local municipality for business tax registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Company Registration together with the Articles of Incorporation (company registration filing instrument) filed under Article 387 of the Companies Act, and the Investment Commission Foreign Investment Approval Certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Taiwan has no statutory minimum paid-up capital for a company limited by shares or for a low-risk wholesale/retail WFOE; however, for a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise, the Investment Commission, MOEA, will assess the business plan and require a paid-up capital that is reasonable and sufficient for the approved scope, including TikTok Shop retail operations. The capital must be remitted from outside Taiwan into a bank account opened in the corporate name, converted into New Taiwan dollars or retained as approved foreign currency, and verified by a bank-issued capital certificate before incorporation registration is completed. There is no mandatory blocked government escrow account; the funds must remain in the company's capital deposit account and may not be withdrawn or disbursed until the Department of Commercial Affairs has issued the Company Registration Certificate. For mainland Chinese investors, the Investment Commission applies additional review criteria under the Act Governing Relations between Peoples of the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area and may impose a higher capitalization requirement for sensitive business lines, although no fixed statutory minimum exists.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [●] LIMITED (THE COMPANY), ADOPTED IN TAIPEI, TAIWAN, ON [●] 20[●]. The full Board, composed of [Name], [Name], and [Name], being lawfully convened with a quorum present, unanimously adopted the following resolutions and recorded them in the minutes. 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. RESOLVED, that the Company’s authorized share capital is established at New Taiwan Dollars [●], divided into [●] ordinary shares, each with par value NT$[●]; that the founding subscribers named on the subscription list hereby subscribe for the entire share capital; that the consideration shall be paid in cash in full to the Company’s bank account before the incorporation registration is filed; and that the directors are jointly and severally authorized to determine capital installment dates, issue share subscription notices, and deliver share certificates after the Company is registered with the Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs, under the Companies Act of Taiwan (R.O.C.). 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, that [●] Bank, [●] Branch, is designated the primary depositary bank; that the Company authorizes the Chairman, the General Manager, and the Chief Financial Officer, acting jointly in any combination of two, to open, operate, and close bank accounts, to sign checks and electronic transfer instructions, to designate online-banking administrators, to apply for foreign-currency accounts necessary for TikTok Shop Payout settlement and Wise B2B payment rails, and to establish authorized-signatory tiers for all financial transactions, subject to an internal wire-transfer limit of NT$[●] requiring board pre-approval above that limit. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE. RESOLVED, that the Company’s registered office is located at [●], Taiwan (R.O.C.); that the Chairman is instructed to execute a commercial lease, install the statutory company nameplate, file the address change with the registry if required, and maintain the registered office open during all business hours as required by law. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed Chairman and statutory director, [Name] is appointed General Manager, [Name] is appointed Company Secretary, and [Name] is appointed statutory auditor, each to serve until the next annual general meeting or until removal by lawful resolution; the officers are authorized and instructed to prepare and file the incorporation registration application, to submit all forms to the central and local tax authorities, to credential the Company on TikTok Shop and Wise, and to exercise all powers necessary to bring the Company into lawful operation. 5. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, that any director, officer, attorney-in-fact, or CPA designated by the Chairman is authorized to make all required applications, pay all fees, collect the Company Registration Certificate, and take all actions necessary or appropriate to effect the foregoing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Screening and Approval for Wholly Foreign-Owned Entity
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan (R.O.C.), through the Invest Taiwan one-stop online application portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Foreign Investment Application and a declaration that the investment derives from the approved investor group for ISIC 4791 TikTok Shop social-commerce retail. Provide the draft Articles of Incorporation, business plan, capital plan, shareholder identification, and a mainland-China-investor declaration where applicable because the source country is mainland China. The Investment Commission will verify that the proposed business is not on the negative list for mainland Chinese investment and that the paid-up capital corresponds to the projected operating scale. Engage a Taiwan-licensed certified public accountant to attest the land/tenant evidence and the capital remittance path before submission. After approval, the Commission issues a Foreign Investment Approval Certificate; this certificate is a condition precedent to later bank remittance and company registration.
required_dossiers: Completed Foreign Investment Application Form
Business plan and operating scope description for ISIC 4791 and TikTok Shop retail
Draft Articles of Incorporation
Certified copies of shareholder identity documents or corporate registry extracts of investor
Power of attorney in favor of local agent/CPA
Proof of source of funds or bank reference letter
Mainland-China investor declaration and group structure chart
Negative-list compliance certificate from a Taiwan attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, file supplementary responses within 30 calendar days of the deficiency notice; if suspended or refused, apply for reconsideration with the Investment Commission within 30 days, requesting a hearing and arguing that social-commerce retail under ISIC 4791 is outside the restricted negative-list industries; upon final refusal, file an administrative appeal with the Executive Yuan within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Notarization/Attestation of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, MOEA Company Name Reservation System; local notary public or law firm authorized to attest signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Reserve the proposed company name through the MOEA online Company Name Reservation System. Choose the exact business scope code 4791 and confirm that the Chinese and English names do not conflict with existing trademarks or registered companies. Prepare final Articles of Incorporation setting out limited liability, capital structure, board powers, registered office, and the operation of online retail. For a WFOE, the investor's signature must be notarized in the home jurisdiction and authenticated by the Taipei Economic and Cultural Office (TECO) or equivalent mission before the documents are submitted in Taiwan. Alternatively, the local CPA may participate in the online attestation session. Retain the name reservation certificate because it must be attached to the final registration application.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application and certificate
Final Articles of Incorporation in Chinese with an English translation
Notarized/attested director and shareholder signature pages
Foreign shareholder authentication certificate from TECO/overseas notary
Power of attorney for the local incorporation agent
CPA attestation letter for Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for conflict or confusing similarity, file an alternative name reservation immediately and do not lose the priority date; if notarization is rejected, correct the signature certificate and re-submit within 14 days; if the registry suspends the attestation, cure the defects and obtain a new certification letter from the attesting CPA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Remittance, Bank Account Opening and Capital Certificate Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Onshore commercial bank licensed by the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC), operating under the Central Bank of Taiwan foreign-exchange regulations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary foreign-investment capital deposit account in the proposed company name using the Investment Commission Approval Certificate and the draft Articles of Incorporation. Remit the subscribed capital from outside Taiwan through the investor's bank and convert into New Taiwan dollars at the prevailing exchange rate. Instruct the bank to issue a Capital Certificate stating the amount, date, and account numbers; the certificate must be printed on bank letterhead and signed by an authorized officer. In parallel, open the operational corporate account and configure it to receive TikTok Shop Payout remittances and Wise B2B transfers. Provide KYC documents, beneficial ownership disclosure, and board resolution authorizing account signatories. Do not disburse or repatriate funds until after the company receives its registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Investment Commission Foreign Investment Approval Certificate
Capital remittance application and source-of-funds documentation
Bank KYC/beneficial ownership forms
Board resolution authorizing bank accounts and signatories
Passports or corporate identification of all account signatories
Draft Articles of Incorporation and proposed company registration certificate
TikTok Shop and Wise account information for settlement routing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises AML/KYC objections, provide additional source-of-funds and corporate-beneficiary evidence; if the Capital Certificate contains an error, ask the bank to issue a corrected version before filing; if the Central Bank of Taiwan suspends the remittance due to foreign-exchange control review, submit the Investment Commission approval and the import/payment contract to the bank for special approval.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Incorporation Filing and Issuance of Company Registration Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) through the Company Registration Online Application system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation registration package online with the Department of Commercial Affairs after the capital certificate and all attestations are completed. Attach the name reservation certificate, Articles of Incorporation, first board resolution, shareholder/director consent letters, bank capital certificate, Investment Commission approval, and the registration fee payment voucher. The registry will verify the statutory disclosure, corporate name, capital adequacy, registered office, and designated statutory officers under the Companies Act. Upon successful examination, the Department issues the Company Registration Certificate, which grants the Company juridical personality. After issuance, publish the registration details and file the certified copy of the first board resolution in the Company's corporate governance minute book.
required_dossiers: Company incorporation registration application form
Name reservation certificate
Articles of Incorporation and attested signature pages
First Board Resolution items (subscription, banking, office, officers)
Bank capital certificate
Investment Commission Foreign Investment Approval Certificate
Director and auditor consent letters
Company registration fee payment voucher
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a deficiency notice, cure the missing items within 15 calendar days; if the application is suspended, submit a formal response to the Department of Commercial Affairs; if the deadline is missed, re-file with corrected documents and a written explanation; if the Department refuses the registration, file an administrative appeal with the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax, Business License, and E-Commerce Platform Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance; local municipal revenue service office responsible for business tax and distance-selling registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 days after the Company Registration Certificate is issued, apply to the National Taxation Bureau for business tax registration and obtain a tax identification number (TIN). Complete the municipal business registration and register the retail business under the e-commerce/distance-selling category consistent with ISIC 4791. If the Company will hold no inventory, no industrial operating license is required; if physical storage or packing is later adopted, apply for a fire safety inspection and local government building/warehouse clearance. Credential the Company on TikTok Shop Seller Center and Wise using the company registration certificate and TIN. Configure accurate sales-tax invoicing and filing responsibilities, and notify the bank of the final registration certificate to unfreeze the capital account.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate
Business Tax Registration Application Form (Article 28, Business Tax Act)
Lease agreement or ownership certificate for registered office
Identity and specimen signature of the statutory responsible person
First Board Resolution appointing the General Manager and tax filing representative
TikTok Shop Seller Center account details
Wise Business account onboarding documents
TIN application and uniform-invoice registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authority suspends the registration, file an explanatory letter and pay any estimated business tax; if the municipal revenue office requests additional licensing evidence, provide the Company Registration Certificate and a statutory declaration that no industrial license is required; if TikTok Shop or Wise onboarding is blocked, submit the Certificate of Registration and Tax Clearance Certificate to the platform.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable for pure digital and social-commerce retail under ISIC 4791; if the Company later establishes a physical warehouse or packing facility, the competent authority becomes the municipal Public Works Bureau, the local Fire Department, and the Environmental Protection Bureau within Taiwan (R.O.C.).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable – no industrial operating license is required for TikTok Shop retail activity; only the Company Registration Certificate and Business Tax Registration are mandatory. Any incidental low-risk warehouse/felting activity would require municipal building occupancy inspection and fire safety certification, not an industrial operating license.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable; if physical logistics/warehousing is later introduced, the competent agency is the Environmental Protection Administration of the Executive Yuan and the local Environmental Protection Bureau of the special municipality.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable – ISIC 4791 online retail with TikTok Shop live-commerce does not appear on the positive-list categories requiring an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act; no EIA evaluation, environmental registration, or pollution-control permit is required for the initial digital-only commercial model.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable – the digital retail operation will not generate industrial wastewater, volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions, or hazardous waste streams. If warehousing with delivery trucks is added later, the Company must comply with Taiwan’s local air pollution emission standards for vehicles (Euro 5/6 equivalent or Ministry-approved standard), municipal sanitary wastewater connection requirements for any toilet facility, and the Waste Management Act obligation to dispose of packaging and general industrial waste through licensed haulers, with manifests retained for five years.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for a pure online-retail company with no physical premises beyond a registered office. If the Company installs inventory shelving, operates a packing room, or employs workers in a physical work site, a Fire Safety Management Certificate from the local Fire Department and an Occupational Safety and Health Act self-inspection file are required, including structural load verification for storage racks, installation of fire extinguishers and emergency lighting, and a no-smoking/electrical-safety program; high-rise office premises require a report on fire protection equipment by a registered fire professional.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (国家税务总局; STA). Operational portals: nationwide Electronic Taxpayer system (电子税务局, https://etax.chinatax.gov.cn), 12366 Taxpayer Service Platform, and China International Trade Single Window (中国国际贸易单一窗口) for export and customs filings. Local administration is handled by provincial and municipal tax service bureaus. The WFOE's VAT invoicing is monitored through the STA's Golden Tax Phase IV (金税四期) system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Upon incorporation with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), the WFOE is automatically issued a Unified Social Credit Code (统一社会信用代码, USCC), which serves as the statutory taxpayer identification number for all PRC tax purposes. Tax registration is completed through the integrated 'multi-certificate, one entity' procedure; no separate tax registration certificate is issued. The WFOE must then: (i) complete real-name authentication for the legal representative and financial officers; (ii) activate its Electronic Taxpayer account; (iii) complete taxpayer-basic data including banking and accounting details; (iv) apply for invoice quotas and fully digitalized electronic invoice (数电票) activation; (v) obtain a Customs Registration Code (海关收发货人登记编号) via the Customs Single Window for export declarations and export tax refunds; and (vi) register as a Trade Foreign Exchange Receipts/Payments Enterprise (货物贸易外汇收支企业名录) with its designated bank for export proceeds. Foreign shareholders do not need a separate PRC TIN unless they independently derive PRC-source income or create a permanent establishment in China.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise formed under PRC Company Law is tax-resident in the PRC by place of incorporation and is subject to Enterprise Income Tax on worldwide income at the standard 25% rate. It is not a pass-through entity, and no check-the-box or look-through election is available. For VAT purposes it must register; annual taxable sales above CNY 5,000,000 in a 12-month period generally require general VAT taxpayer status, while below that amount it may elect small-scale taxpayer status, which does not alter entity-level income taxation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: PRC law does not provide a US-style check-the-box entity classification election. The material elections available to a PRC WFOE are: (i) VAT taxpayer status election between small-scale taxpayer status (simplified levy, currently reduced to 1% through the applicable transition period; statutory rate 3%) and general VAT taxpayer status where annual taxable sales do not exceed CNY 5,000,000; (ii) export VAT treatment election between 'exempt-and-refundable' treatment and 'exempt-without-refund' treatment for exported goods, including cross-border e-commerce retail exports; (iii) selection of the applicable customs supervision code for cross-border e-commerce export, such as 9610, 9710, 9810 or 1210; and (iv) transfer-pricing documentation and treaty-relief elections for cross-border related-party payments. No hybrid-mismatch or transparent-entity election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (增值税, VAT) and, for applicable consumer goods, consumption tax; export VAT zero-rating and refund are administered by the STA together with the General Administration of Customs (GACC) through the China International Trade Single Window.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No revenue threshold for initial VAT registration; all WFOEs must tax-register upon incorporation. The general VAT taxpayer registration threshold is CNY 5,000,000 of annual taxable sales in a rolling 12-month period. Export registration with the Customs Single Window and cross-border e-commerce export filing have no turnover threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China mandates the use of fully digitalized electronic VAT invoices (数电票) issued through the STA-controlled National VAT Invoice Management System. Invoices are validated and cleared in real time, bear a dynamic QR code, an electronic seal, and a unique platform invoice number, and are delivered through the Electronic Taxpayer system or enterprise APIs connected to the STA platform. Paper and electronic VAT special invoices are also transmitted through the Golden Tax System; no input VAT credit or export refund can be claimed in respect of an invoice not uploaded and verified by the tax authority. Cross-border e-commerce retail exports require transmission of order, payment, and logistics data through the Customs Single Window and the cross-border e-commerce retail export declaration system, with customs clearance data automatically reconciled to tax records.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported from mainland China's customs territory are zero-rated for VAT. A general VAT taxpayer that makes an export sale may claim refund of attributable input VAT provided the transaction is genuine, the goods were actually shipped out of mainland China, export proceeds are collected in foreign exchange, and supporting documentation is complete and internally consistent. Cross-border e-commerce retail export under Customs supervision code 9610, including sales to Taiwan through TikTok Shop, may use 'exempt-without-refund' treatment where the exporter has no valid input VAT invoice for the goods, or 'exempt-and-refund' treatment where goods were purchased with VAT special invoices and the exporter is a general VAT taxpayer. Export sales to Taiwan qualify where the goods actually leave the mainland China customs territory; digital and offshore platform services require separate analysis under the cross-border taxable services rules of Circular 36/2016.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (出口货物报关单) or Cross-Border E-Commerce Retail Export Manifest (跨境电子商务零售出口申报清单/9610 list)
Cross-border e-commerce order data, platform transaction records, and TikTok Shop settlement reports
Payment data including cross-border payment platform settlement reports and Export Proceeds Collection Certificate (银行收汇凭证/涉外收入申报单/Inward Remittance Certificate)
Logistics documentation: Bill of Lading, air waybill, or courier/express delivery manifest showing the goods departed mainland China and were delivered to the Taiwan consignee
Commercial invoice and export packing list
VAT special invoice or purchase invoice of the exported goods where input VAT refund is claimed
China Customs export reconciliation and Electronic Port (电子口岸) records
Foreign exchange collection proof from the designated bank, including the Inward Remittance Certificate or bank settlement/foreign exchange memo, when export refund is claimed
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export refund files are subject to multi-dimensional cross-matching by the STA Golden Tax Phase IV and Customs Single Window: customs declaration, invoice flow, goods flow, foreign-exchange/payment flow, and logistics flow must satisfy 'four-flow consistency'. False export declarations or refund fraud trigger: (i) denial or clawback of the VAT refund; (ii) late-payment interest at 0.05% per day; (iii) administrative penalties under the PRC Tax Collection and Administration Law and Customs Law, generally from 0.5 to 5 times the tax underpaid or refund fraudulently obtained; (iv) customs penalties for false declaration; and (v) criminal liability under PRC Criminal Law Article 204 for fraudulently obtaining export tax refunds, punishable by fines, confiscation of property, and imprisonment up to life sentence where the amount is especially large. Tax authorities may retroactively recover the clawed-back tax for up to ten years in fraud cases and may permanently disqualify the WFOE from future export zero-rating or revoke its Customs Registration Code.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China and State Administration of Foreign Exchange for mainland China; Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan), Financial Supervisory Commission, and Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs for Taiwan-side capital, banking, and outbound-investment controls. The State Administration of Foreign Exchange is the principal mainland foreign-exchange administration authority, while the People's Bank of China supervises the monetary and payment-system framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The renminbi is generally convertible for bona fide current-account transactions, including permitted trade payments, service payments, salary payments, taxes, and documented profit distributions. Capital-account transactions remain regulated and are subject to registration, bank review, approved purposes, foreign-investment rules, debt limits, and applicable macro-prudential controls. A WFOE may generally remit dividends, liquidation proceeds, and other permitted returns of capital after completion of statutory audit, tax filing and payment, reserve allocations, board or shareholder approval, and supporting-document review by the handling bank. Banks commonly require evidence of distributable profits, audited financial statements, tax clearance or tax filing records, resolution approving the distribution, and confirmation that registered capital, intercompany loans, and other foreign-exchange registrations are compliant. Payments to or from Taiwan may also be subject to cross-Strait investment, trade, banking, prohibited-counterparty, sanctions-screening, and reporting restrictions. The entity must not assume that a Taiwan-based shareholder, payment provider, or settlement account can bypass mainland foreign-exchange, customs, tax, or payment rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Mainland China does not generally impose a universal mandatory surrender ratio or an automatic fixed-period conversion requirement for all export proceeds. Exporters may generally retain foreign currency in permitted foreign-exchange accounts and may settle foreign currency with a bank when commercially required, subject to genuine-transaction review and applicable account limits. Goods-trade foreign-exchange receipts remain subject to customs, tax, banking, and foreign-exchange monitoring, including consistency among contracts, invoices, customs declarations, logistics records, and payment data. Banks may require collection of export proceeds within the contractual and regulatory period and may investigate overdue, abnormal, advance, related-party, third-party, split, or mismatched receipts. If the WFOE is only a domestic or platform retailer and does not act as exporter of record, export-proceeds rules generally apply to the actual exporter and settlement party rather than automatically to the WFOE. Any Taiwan-side exporter or investor must separately comply with Taiwan foreign-exchange reporting and Mainland-area transaction restrictions. Mandatory conversion ratios, if introduced for a specific pilot, account type, sector, or enforcement action, must be confirmed with the designated bank and current SAFE rules before implementation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for collection, treasury support, and permitted business payments; Low as a substitute for a mainland corporate bank. An offshore electronic-money institution, including Wise or a similar provider, generally cannot open a mainland RMB corporate deposit account, perform unrestricted domestic payment clearing, hold regulated customer deposits in China, receive or convert foreign-investment capital as a substitute for a designated bank, or independently determine the legality of cross-border trade payments. Use is viable only where the provider accepts the WFOE, the payer and beneficiary are correctly identified, the transaction has a genuine underlying purpose, the payment route is permitted, and the provider's licensing and geographic terms cover China-related transactions. TikTok Shop payouts must be contracted, invoiced, and settled through an account and payment route accepted by the platform and compliant with mainland tax, foreign-exchange, data, and bank requirements. Funds should not be routed through personal accounts, undisclosed third parties, nominee accounts, or accounts inconsistent with the WFOE's registered business model.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding may be available for selected banks and low-risk cases, but it is not guaranteed. Mainland banks normally require verification of the legal representative, authorized signatory, ultimate beneficial owner, actual controller, registered address, business premises, tax status, source and use of funds, and expected transaction profile. In-person appearance, face-to-face video verification, an on-site visit, specimen-signature verification, or a local branch interview may be required, particularly for a newly incorporated WFOE, a foreign shareholder, a Taiwan-linked ownership chain, cross-border collection, foreign-exchange accounts, capital accounts, high-volume platform payouts, or unusual payment flows. Directors do not universally have to appear physically, but the bank may require the legal representative or authorized signatory to attend and may reject powers of attorney that do not satisfy its internal control requirements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Taiwan-linked ownership, control, funding, or payment counterparties without a documented cross-Strait legal basis.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified constitutional documents for the WFOE and shareholder; complete ownership chart through all intermediate entities to the natural-person ultimate beneficial owner; Taiwan-side investment approval, filing, or exemption analysis; identity and address evidence for controllers; sanctions and restricted-party screening record; transaction-purpose memorandum; shareholder funding agreement; and bank-specific cross-Strait compliance confirmations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent business profile: registered social-commerce retail scope but projected high-value imports, exports, advertising receipts, marketplace payouts, or financial flows unrelated to the registered scope.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business model memorandum; platform contracts; supplier and customer agreements; product catalogue; invoices; logistics and warehouse contracts; customs registrations where applicable; tax registration; projected monthly transaction matrix by currency and country; expected counterparties; and a documented process for amending business scope or obtaining licenses if regulated activities arise.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: TikTok Shop or marketplace payouts received from a payment processor, platform affiliate, or third-party settlement entity rather than the contractual platform counterparty.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform master agreement; payout-policy documents; merchant account certificate; settlement-flow diagram; platform-issued statements; contractual chain identifying the payer; invoices and reconciliation reports; tax treatment memorandum; beneficial-owner confirmation; and bank approval for third-party or centralized settlement where required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of Wise or another offshore EMI as the primary operating account or as a channel for RMB capital injection.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provider licensing evidence; account ownership confirmation in the WFOE's legal name; provider terms permitting China-related corporate payments; source-of-funds records; underlying invoices and contracts; payment-purpose classification; transaction limits; reconciliation policy; and a written bank or counsel confirmation that the route does not replace required mainland bank, SAFE, customs, or tax procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign-investment capital received before completion of the WFOE's registration, bank account setup, capital reporting, or required shareholder documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business licence; foreign-investment information report; articles of association; shareholder resolution; capital contribution schedule; capital-account registration or bank filing evidence where applicable; capital verification or bank credit evidence; remitter and beneficiary identity records; SWIFT confirmation; source-of-funds evidence; and capital-use budget.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner, actual controller, director, signatory, supplier, or customer located in a sanctioned, high-risk, or restricted jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Passport and corporate identity documents; independent ownership verification; sanctions, adverse-media, and politically exposed person screening; jurisdictional risk assessment; enhanced due-diligence questionnaire; written legal analysis of applicable sanctions and export controls; transaction-level approvals; and contractual representations, warranties, audit rights, and termination rights.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent split payments, rapid pass-through transfers, round-dollar payments, unexplained refunds, personal-account settlements, or payment amounts inconsistent with invoices.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three-way reconciliation among contract, invoice, and bank statement; payment approval matrix; refund and chargeback policy; customer and supplier master files; transaction-monitoring alerts; explanations for variances; evidence of delivery or platform fulfilment; and documented prohibition of personal or nominee accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Import or export data inconsistent with customs declarations, VAT invoices, logistics records, or foreign-exchange receipts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial contracts; purchase orders; commercial invoices; customs declarations; bills of lading or courier records; warehouse receipts; proof of delivery; VAT special invoices where applicable; foreign-exchange receipt records; reconciliation schedule; and exception reports approved by finance and compliance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Requested outward dividend, service-fee, royalty, loan repayment, or related-party payment without tax and transfer-pricing support.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board or shareholder approval; audited accounts; tax returns and payment certificates; distributable-profit calculation; intercompany agreement; transfer-pricing analysis; withholding-tax review; beneficial-owner treaty analysis where relevant; evidence of actual services or licensed intellectual property; invoice; and bank remittance application.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Virtual office, unverifiable operating location, nominee director, dormant-company profile, or inability to demonstrate personnel and operating capacity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease or ownership evidence; photographs and bank site-visit materials; payroll and social-insurance records; employment contracts; supplier and warehouse arrangements; operating permits; management biographies; board minutes; accounting-system evidence; and a written explanation of any outsourced fulfilment or platform-based operating model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Data, cybersecurity, or platform arrangements that create uncertainty over cross-border transfer of customer, payment, or transaction data.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Data-flow map; privacy notices; processing agreements; cybersecurity controls; data-minimization policy; access-control matrix; localization and cross-border-transfer assessment; platform compliance certifications; incident-response plan; and bank-approved method for supplying transaction evidence without unlawful data export.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route shareholder capital from an account held in the documented shareholder's legal name to the WFOE's designated foreign-investment capital account or other bank account approved for foreign-investment capital. Confirm before remittance that the shareholder, beneficiary, currency, capital purpose, amount, and remitter bank details match the WFOE registration and bank records. Use a SWIFT wire with accurate legal names, registration numbers where supported, bank identifiers, purpose narrative, and charges instruction. Retain the MT103 or ISO 20022 pacs.008 confirmation, credit advice, exchange-rate record, capital contribution resolution, source-of-funds evidence, and bank settlement or SAFE-related records. Do not mix registered capital, shareholder loans, trade receipts, platform revenue, and operating cash in a manner that obscures purpose. Shareholder loans require separate foreign-debt registration, quota, macro-prudential, or bank-processing analysis. Capital settlement should be conducted only for genuine business expenditure and within applicable foreign-exchange rules; avoid cash withdrawals, payments to unrelated parties, personal-account transfers, and circular flows.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use the WFOE's mainland operational account for RMB domestic payments and its permitted foreign-exchange account for documented cross-border payments. For ordinary supplier, logistics, software, advertising, and service payments, use a bank wire supported by contract, invoice, tax analysis, proof of performance, and any required customs or withholding documentation. The bank may process a legacy SWIFT MT103 or its ISO 20022 successor, pacs.008, depending on the bank and correspondent route. For higher-risk or documentary trade, use a commercial letter of credit issued or advised through an eligible bank under UCP 600, with documentary requirements aligned to the purchase contract. Import payments should match customs and logistics records where applicable; service payments should identify the service period, place of performance, tax treatment, and beneficiary; royalties and related-party charges require additional substance and withholding-tax review. TikTok Shop payouts and marketplace settlements should be reconciled to platform statements, customer orders, refunds, chargebacks, VAT records, and the contractual settlement entity before funds are transferred cross-border. Taiwan-related payments require additional screening against cross-Strait restrictions and should not be processed solely on the basis of a generic invoice.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards for genuine underlying trade, receivable, payable, dividend, or other permitted exposure, subject to bank suitability review, documentation of the underlying transaction, approved credit line, tenor limits, and settlement procedures.

Non-deliverable forwards may be available through qualified mainland banks for permitted currencies and genuine exposure, subject to current regulatory authorization, bank risk limits, product eligibility, and evidence that the transaction is a hedge rather than speculative trading.

Currency swaps or cross-currency swaps may be available to eligible corporate customers for documented financing or operating exposures, subject to bank approval, master agreements, collateral or credit support, accounting treatment, and applicable foreign-exchange and derivatives rules.

Foreign-exchange options, collars, and structured hedges may be available only where the bank confirms product eligibility, suitability, disclosure, and genuine-risk requirements; complex leveraged or speculative structures should be prohibited under the treasury policy unless separately approved by the board and counsel.

Permitted hedges should be supported by a rolling exposure schedule, hedge-designation policy, counterparty limits, confirmation matching, valuation controls, collateral monitoring, independent settlement verification, and monthly effectiveness review. Hedging should not be used to create unregistered capital inflows, conceal beneficial ownership, or transfer value to an unrelated third party.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Company Act Section 22-1 Filing of Major Shareholder, Director, Supervisor and Manager Information (年度董監事暨主要股東申報)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (Taiwan)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March for the preceding calendar-year reporting period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-exempt non-public companies failing to file within the statutory deadline expose the responsible person to administrative fines; the competent authority may impose per-instance fines until the filing is remediated. Persistent non-compliance can trigger a corporate governance inspection and possible administrative dissolution procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Annual Settlement Return (營利事業所得稅結算申報)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau (jurisdictional office), Ministry of Finance, Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 May of the following year for the prior calendar year; a one-month extension to 30 June applies where financial statements are certified by a Taiwan CPA.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers default tax assessment. Filing after a reminder notice incurs a 10% delinquency surcharge on the assessed tax; continued failure after the reminder period incurs a 20% surcharge plus daily interest on unpaid tax. Long-term non-filing may lead to enforced collection and suspension of business-related registration privileges.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Undistributed Earnings Surtax Return and Payment (未分配盈餘申報)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau (jurisdictional office), Ministry of Finance, Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed together with the annual income tax settlement return by 31 May, or by 30 June where the CPA-certified extension is elected.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under-declared retained earnings are subject to the statutory 5% undistributed-earnings surtax and related underpayment penalties. Late payment accrues daily interest, and amounts remaining unpaid after the statutory demand period may be referred to tax enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign/Mainland Investor Operating Status Report (投資事業營運狀況申報)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (Taiwan)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 June, reporting the immediately preceding fiscal year's operating and financial status.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or false reporting may result in administrative fines, revisions to the approved investment status, and adverse effects on future applications for profit remittance, foreign-exchange settlement, capital repatriation, or investment extension.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholders' Meeting Approval of Business Report and Financial Statements (股東常會承認)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company shareholders' meeting; certified minutes are retained in the statutory minute book and no direct regulatory filing is required unless amendments are involved.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the close of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year company, by 30 June unless an extension is granted by the competent authority.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Holding the meeting after the statutory six-month period exposes the responsible person to administrative fines. Failure to approve financial statements prevents lawful dividend distribution and may impair future foreign-exchange remittance applications.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory independent audit by a Taiwan-certified public accountant is required for public companies, companies whose paid-in capital meets the threshold prescribed by the Ministry of Economic Affairs (generally NT$30 million and above), and companies designated by the competent authority. Smaller non-public companies with no accumulated deficit may prepare unaudited financial statements unless shareholders request an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Public companies apply IFRS as endorsed by the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC). Non-public companies apply the Business Entity Accounting Act and the associated Taiwan Business Accounting Standards/GAAP, which are substantially aligned with IFRS for small- and medium-sized entities.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 20% Taiwan corporate income tax on taxable income. A separate 5% undistributed earnings tax may apply to qualifying retained post-tax earnings not distributed or otherwise utilized.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Taiwan generally provides no broad corporate tax holiday for ordinary social-commerce retail. Qualifying enterprises may claim industry-specific incentives under the Statute for Industrial Innovation, including an investment tax credit for qualifying research and development expenditure, subject to statutory conditions and approval or filing requirements. Small enterprises may qualify for simplified assessment rules only where statutory conditions are met. Taiwan-source dividends, interest, royalties, and service income paid to nonresidents may be subject to withholding tax rather than ordinary resident corporate income tax treatment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Taiwan Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return (營利事業所得稅結算申報書), filed through the Ministry of Finance eTax electronic filing system or the taxpayer's local National Taxation Bureau. The applicable local bureau depends on the company's registered head office or fixed place of business.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with a separate provisional income tax filing generally required for qualifying companies during 1 September through 30 September. A company may generally elect annual accounting-year filing only where statutory eligibility and approval requirements are satisfied.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year company, annual income tax returns are generally due from 1 May through 31 May of the following year. The provisional return is generally due during 1 September through 30 September of the current year. If the deadline falls on a non-business day, the deadline is extended to the next business day. A company using a non-calendar fiscal year generally files within five months after fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the unified business number, legal name, registered address, accounting period, paid-in capital, responsible person, accounting method, and filing status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Taiwan company is a resident taxpayer for Taiwan corporate income tax purposes. A nonresident shareholder is not entered as the taxpayer unless separately filing Taiwan-source income; its Taiwan-source dividend, interest, royalty, or service income is generally reported through withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Total revenue and gross receipts section
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report gross merchandise sales, platform sales, affiliate or commission income, shipping income, rebates, returns, discounts, and other operating revenue on an accrual basis under Taiwan tax and accounting rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile TikTok Shop or other platform settlement reports to Taiwan invoices, bank receipts, payment processor statements, and the general ledger. Gross-versus-net presentation must reflect the company's contractual role as principal or agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Cost of goods sold and operating expense section
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report inventory purchases, import costs, freight, customs charges, warehousing, payment processing fees, platform commissions, advertising, employee costs, rent, depreciation, and other deductible expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to nonresidents require source-based withholding analysis. Deductibility requires commercial purpose, supporting documents, proper invoices or equivalent evidence, and compliance with withholding and transfer-pricing rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjust accounting profit for non-deductible expenses, exempt income, separately taxed income, tax penalties, unsubstantiated expenses, excessive related-party charges, provisions not permitted for tax purposes, and other statutory differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not deduct shareholder distributions, income tax, undocumented related-party charges, or expenses that are not arm's-length or are unsupported by contracts, invoices, delivery evidence, or business-purpose records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identify related parties, transaction categories, transaction values, pricing methods, counterparties, and required transfer-pricing documentation. Disclose cross-border purchases, sales, royalties, management services, financing, guarantees, and cost allocations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Transactions with the China parent, affiliates, offshore procurement companies, logistics providers, platform entities, and financing parties must be tested under Taiwan's arm's-length rules. Taiwan cannot be treated as a mere booking location without functions, assets, and risk evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Taxable income and corporate income tax computation section
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute taxable income after tax adjustments, apply the 20% corporate income tax rate, deduct eligible tax credits and foreign tax credits, and reconcile installments or withholding credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are limited by Taiwan statutory rules and generally require proof of foreign tax payment, income attribution, and prescribed documentation. China-source income requires separate cross-strait tax analysis and cannot automatically be treated as Taiwan-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Determine whether post-tax earnings retained after the statutory utilization period are subject to the additional 5% undistributed earnings tax and report qualifying capital expenditures, investments, or other permitted utilization.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign shareholder's decision not to distribute profits does not by itself eliminate the Taiwan undistributed earnings analysis. Dividend declarations, capitalization, loss offsets, and permitted reinvestment must be documented.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Tax payable, payment, refund, and signature section
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report tax payable, provisional payments, withholding credits, foreign tax credits, refund claims, payment details, responsible person certification, and preparer information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Refunds and credit claims require consistent bank, withholding, ledger, and tax-return records. A nonresident shareholder must receive dividends only after corporate approvals, distributable-profit calculations, and applicable withholding procedures.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without tax payable may result in an administrative penalty generally up to NT$30,000, subject to statutory conditions. Late filing with tax payable may attract a surcharge generally equal to 10% of tax payable, subject to statutory minimum and maximum amounts. Failure to file may result in assessment by the tax authority, a penalty generally up to 20% of assessed tax, and loss of certain deductions or tax benefits. Late tax payment generally attracts a 1% surcharge for each two-day period, subject to a statutory maximum, followed by interest and compulsory collection. False reporting, omitted sales, false invoices, or deliberate tax evasion may create criminal exposure.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% on dividends paid by a Taiwan company to a nonresident shareholder, subject to applicable tax treaty or cross-strait relief. Taiwan does not have a conventional comprehensive income tax treaty with Mainland China; Taiwan-China tax treatment is governed by cross-strait legislation and applicable administrative rules rather than a standard bilateral DTA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain the recipient's tax-residency certificate or other prescribed evidence, confirm beneficial ownership and treaty eligibility, classify the payment correctly, and apply for any required advance approval from the relevant National Taxation Bureau. Where relief is unavailable at source, withhold at the domestic rate and pursue refund or adjustment under the applicable procedure. Maintain shareholder registers, board or shareholder resolutions, dividend vouchers, payment records, tax-residency evidence, beneficial-ownership evidence, and anti-conduit analysis. A China-resident recipient cannot claim Taiwan treaty relief merely by presenting a Mainland China tax certificate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Taiwan-source royalties and interest paid to nonresidents are generally subject to 20% withholding tax, subject to statutory exemptions, prescribed reductions, or an applicable tax agreement. Interest on specified government-approved loans, qualifying financing, or other legally defined categories may have different rates. Royalties may also require source-of-income, Taiwan usage, permanent-establishment, and beneficial-owner analysis. Payments to Mainland China recipients require separate cross-strait tax treatment and should not be reduced without written legal support and tax authority confirmation where required.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Taiwan generally requires a Local File where annual revenue is at least NT$300 million or where controlled transactions exceed prescribed categories and thresholds, commonly NT$200 million for purchases or sales of tangible goods and NT$100 million for other controlled transactions, subject to current regulations and transaction aggregation rules. A Master File is generally required where the Taiwan entity belongs to a multinational enterprise group meeting the prescribed consolidated-revenue threshold, commonly NT$3 billion, together with applicable Taiwan filing conditions. Country-by-Country reporting generally applies to qualifying ultimate parent or surrogate-parent groups with consolidated revenue of at least NT$27 billion.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Other methods permitted under Taiwan transfer-pricing regulations where the prescribed methods cannot reasonably be applied and the alternative method is supported by reliable evidence
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan does not operate a single UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime applicable to all entities. Substance is nevertheless enforced through corporate income tax, transfer-pricing, controlled-foreign-company, beneficial-ownership, anti-avoidance, permanent-establishment, and business-purpose rules. The Taiwan entity must demonstrate real functions, personnel, premises, decision-making, assets, risks, inventory control, customer activity, and commercially supportable pricing. A company that merely receives TikTok Shop proceeds while strategic decisions, procurement, inventory, marketing, and risk control remain outside Taiwan may face income reallocation, denial of deductions, withholding reassessment, permanent-establishment findings, or general anti-avoidance challenges.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Jurisdictional misclassification and unauthorized operating structure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Mainland China WFOE registration or tax identity to conduct Taiwan retail, warehousing, payment collection, hiring, or platform operations without a Taiwan-registered entity, branch, local agent, or other legally valid structure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Possible denial of business registration, tax registration, deductions, and input tax credits; assessment of unpaid corporate income tax and business tax; administrative fines under tax, company, foreign-investment, labor, customs, and foreign-exchange rules; and orders to cease or regularize operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible persons may face administrative penalties, tax collection proceedings, civil liability for unpaid taxes and creditor losses, and criminal exposure where conduct involves intentional evasion, false registration, document falsification, or unauthorized business activity. Travel restrictions or imprisonment are not automatic and require statutory grounds and competent-authority or judicial action.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Suppressing TikTok Shop sales, omitting platform settlements, fabricating expenses, diverting revenue to offshore affiliates, concealing inventory, or submitting false tax records to reduce Taiwan taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, back tax, interest, administrative penalties, and potential criminal prosecution under the Taiwan Tax Collection Act. Deliberate evasion by fraud or other unlawful means may carry imprisonment of up to five years and a criminal fine of up to NT$10 million, subject to the applicable provision and court determination.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible persons and persons who directly participated may incur criminal liability, civil restitution, tax recovery, and director disqualification consequences. Company status does not shield individuals who ordered, approved, or knowingly implemented the evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Business tax and false invoice violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to issue Taiwan uniform invoices, issuing invoices for non-existent transactions, claiming input tax on sham purchases, misclassifying platform commissions, or using another entity's invoices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Business tax assessment, interest, penalties that may be calculated by reference to the evaded tax, denial of input credits, invoice restrictions, and potential criminal liability for aggravated or fraudulent conduct under the Business Tax Act and related criminal provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible persons, accounting personnel, and transaction participants may be jointly exposed to administrative and criminal proceedings where they knowingly created or used false documents. Civil recovery may include unpaid tax, penalties, unjust enrichment, and damages.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length procurement prices, inflated royalties or management fees, guaranteed losses for the Taiwan entity, undocumented cost allocations, or shifting TikTok Shop margin to a low-substance affiliate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax authority adjustment to arm's-length income, denial of deductions, withholding reassessment, interest, documentation penalties, and possible penalties for inaccurate or incomplete disclosures. Taiwan may use available information, comparables, customs data, platform data, and economic substance evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may face civil liability to the company or shareholders for approving non-commercial transactions and may face criminal exposure if transfer-pricing entries are part of deliberate tax fraud, false accounting, money laundering, or asset diversion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Illegal profit repatriation and withholding failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, interest, service fees, or management charges to Mainland China or offshore recipients without proper corporate approvals, withholding, residency analysis, exchange-control documentation, or beneficial-owner verification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Withholding-tax reassessment, payer liability for tax not withheld, interest, penalties, denial of deductions, foreign-exchange or company-law sanctions, and possible restrictions on future remittances. Improper distributions may be recoverable from recipients and responsible directors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for unlawful distributions, breach of fiduciary duties, unpaid withholding tax, and company losses. Criminal consequences may arise for falsified approvals, concealed distributions, asset misappropriation, or intentional tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Customs, import valuation, and inventory diversion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Under-invoicing imports, misdescribing goods, splitting shipments to evade controls, diverting imported inventory to Taiwan sales without customs and tax records, or using related-party transfer prices inconsistent with customs valuation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Customs reassessment, duties and business tax, administrative fines, seizure or forfeiture, import restrictions, and criminal prosecution for smuggling or fraudulent declarations where statutory thresholds and intent are established.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible persons and customs declarants may face civil liability, administrative sanctions, and criminal liability. Directors may be pursued where they authorized or knowingly tolerated the conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-money laundering and prohibited payment flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using Wise, platform wallets, nominee accounts, unrelated third-party payees, split payments, fictitious suppliers, or circular settlements to conceal beneficial ownership, move proceeds, or bypass banking and cross-strait controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Account blocking, transaction rejection, enhanced due diligence, reporting to competent authorities, confiscation, AML administrative penalties, and criminal money-laundering liability. Taiwan's Money Laundering Control Act may impose imprisonment of up to seven years and criminal fines up to NT$50 million for qualifying money-laundering conduct, subject to statutory elements and amendments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals who know, facilitate, arrange, or benefit from laundering may face imprisonment, fines, confiscation, civil restitution, and asset freezing. Directors may also face travel restrictions where legally ordered; such restrictions are not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False books, fabricated contracts, and accounting obstruction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Backdating intercompany agreements, altering platform reports, creating sham invoices, concealing related parties, destroying accounting records, or obstructing a tax audit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disallowance of deductions, estimated assessment, administrative penalties, evidence-preservation orders, and possible criminal liability under tax, accounting, company, forgery, or obstruction provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, responsible persons, accountants, and employees may be personally prosecuted where they participated in falsification or obstruction. Civil claims may include tax losses, investigation costs, penalties, and shareholder or creditor damages.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits without distributable retained earnings, distributing before statutory accounts or approvals, concealing losses, returning capital as dividends, or transferring company assets to shareholders at undervalue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recipient recovery, director liability for restoration of distributed amounts, tax reassessment, penalties, and potential company-law or insolvency-related criminal consequences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly or personally liable for restitution and damages. Imprisonment or travel restrictions require a separate statutory offense, judicial process, and applicable evidence; they do not arise solely from an ordinary defective dividend.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Permanent establishment and unregistered local presence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating Taiwan sales, fulfillment, customer service, inventory, or contracting activities through personnel or agents while claiming that all business is performed offshore and that no Taiwan taxable presence exists.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Attribution of Taiwan-source profits, corporate income tax and business tax assessments, withholding obligations, interest, penalties, and possible registration or licensing enforcement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may face civil liability for tax and regulatory losses and criminal exposure only where the underlying conduct independently constitutes intentional evasion, fraud, falsification, or another offense.
